Privacy

Search should reveal as little about you as practical.

The guide is designed to help people find support without exposing individual search histories or typed addresses to providers.

Address and distance search

If you enter a home, work, or other starting address, your browser sends that address to the address-lookup service so it can be converted to coordinates for distance filtering. The Treasure Valley Mental Health Guide does not place the typed address into provider analytics or show it to providers.

Because the address lookup is performed by a third-party geocoding service, that service may process the request under its own terms and privacy practices. Before public launch, the guide should use a production-ready geocoding arrangement with documented privacy terms.

Provider analytics

Advanced provider analytics use aggregated event data such as profile views, outbound clicks, structured specialty or modality filters, general city filters, visit type, insurance selection, and referral source. Providers do not receive raw free-text mental health searches or the visitor’s typed starting address.

The browser stores a random anonymous visitor identifier so repeated visits can be counted more accurately without using the visitor’s name or email address.

Provider accounts

Provider account authentication and provider profile data are stored through the project’s connected Supabase services. Provider information intended for publication is displayed in the directory; account credentials are not public.

No client medical records

This guide is not a therapy client portal or electronic health record. Visitors should not submit medical records, psychotherapy notes, or confidential clinical information through directory search fields.
